steps.name: Coupling types and CLI subcommand
steps.criteria: GIVEN a user runs `barad-dur coupling <root-dir>`, WHEN the root-dir argument is provided, THEN the CLI parses the coupling subcommand with default config values (24h coupling window, 6-month time window, 30.0 min-coupling threshold, CLI output format). GIVEN a user runs `barad-dur coupling` without arguments, THEN an error message indicates the root-dir is required. GIVEN existing subcommands (analyze, backfill, init, gate), WHEN any is invoked, THEN behavior is unchanged.

steps.name: Repository discovery
steps.criteria: GIVEN a root directory containing subdirectories, WHEN discover_repos is called, THEN directories with a valid `.git` folder and at least one commit are returned as discovered repos, AND directories without `.git` or with no commits are returned as skipped with appropriate reasons (NotAGitRepo, NoCommits). GIVEN a root directory with no subdirectories, THEN the discovered list is empty and no error occurs. GIVEN a subdirectory with unreadable permissions, THEN it appears in the skipped list with a PermissionDenied reason.

steps.name: Parallel snapshot collection with skip-blame
steps.criteria: GIVEN a list of discovered repos, WHEN snapshots are collected for coupling analysis, THEN each repo produces a RepoSnapshot with commits and authors populated, AND blame_map is empty (skip-blame optimization), AND repos that fail collection appear in the skipped list with a CollectionFailed reason rather than aborting the entire pipeline. GIVEN 3 or more repos, THEN collection completes faster than sequential execution (parallel via rayon).

steps.name: Temporal coupling analysis and CLI rendering
steps.criteria: GIVEN two repos where commits overlap within a 24h window at least 3 times, WHEN temporal coupling is computed, THEN the pair appears in the report with a temporal score equal to (co_changes / min(commits_a, commits_b)) * 100, AND confidence is HIGH for 30+ co-changes, MEDIUM for 10-29, LOW for 3-9. GIVEN two repos with fewer than 3 co-changes within the window, THEN the pair does not appear in the report. GIVEN the CLI output format, WHEN the report is rendered, THEN pairs are displayed in a ranked table sorted by temporal score descending, with repo names, score, co-changes, and confidence columns. GIVEN a complete pipeline (discovery through rendering), WHEN `barad-dur coupling <root-dir>` is run end-to-end, THEN a CLI table is printed to stdout.

phases.name: Team and Dependency Coupling with JSON Output

steps.name: Team coupling analysis
steps.criteria: GIVEN two repos with overlapping authors (matched by lowercase display name), WHEN team coupling is computed, THEN the pair's team score equals (shared_authors / total_unique_authors) * 100, AND shared author names are listed. GIVEN exactly one shared author between two repos, THEN is_single_bridge is true and bridge_author contains that author's name. GIVEN two repos with no shared authors, THEN the team score is 0.0 and shared_authors is empty.

steps.name: Dependency coupling analysis
steps.criteria: GIVEN two repos whose Cargo.toml files share dependencies, WHEN dependency coupling is computed, THEN shared_deps lists the common dependency names and shared_count reflects the count. GIVEN repo A's Cargo.toml lists repo B as a path or git dependency, THEN direct_dependency is populated with from=A and to=B. GIVEN repos with package.json, go.mod, or requirements.txt manifests, THEN shared dependencies are detected from those formats as well. GIVEN the coupling report includes blast_radius entries, THEN hub dependencies consumed by 3+ repos are listed with their consumer repos and count.

steps.name: Combined scoring and JSON output
steps.criteria: GIVEN all three coupling dimensions are available for a pair, WHEN the combined score is computed, THEN it equals temporal * 0.50 + team * 0.25 + dependency * 0.25. GIVEN custom weights are provided via config, THEN the formula uses those weights instead of defaults. GIVEN --json flag is passed to the coupling subcommand, WHEN the report is rendered, THEN output is valid JSON with a top-level `coupling` key containing schema_version=1, repos_scanned, pairs_analyzed, pairs array, and blast_radius array. GIVEN --json --pretty flags, THEN the JSON output is pretty-printed. GIVEN --json -o <path>, THEN the JSON is written to the specified file path.

steps.name: Interactive force-directed graph
steps.criteria: GIVEN --html flag is passed to the coupling subcommand, WHEN the report is rendered, THEN a self-contained HTML file is produced with all CSS and JS inlined (no external dependencies). GIVEN the HTML output, WHEN opened in a browser, THEN a force-directed graph displays repos as nodes and coupling pairs as edges, with edge thickness proportional to the combined coupling score. GIVEN the graph, WHEN hovering over a node, THEN the repo name and its coupling pair count are shown. GIVEN --html -o <path>, THEN the HTML file is written to the specified path. GIVEN --html --open, THEN the file is written and opened in the default browser.

steps.name: Coupling matrix and dimension filtering
steps.criteria: GIVEN the HTML output, WHEN the Matrix tab is selected, THEN an NxN heatmap grid displays coupling scores between all repo pairs, with color intensity proportional to score. GIVEN the HTML output, WHEN dimension filter checkboxes (temporal, team, dependency) are toggled, THEN the graph and matrix update to show only the selected dimensions in the combined score recalculation. GIVEN all dimensions are unchecked, THEN all pairs show zero scores. GIVEN only temporal is checked, THEN scores reflect only the temporal dimension.
